questions.question: P, Q and R together have 180 candies among them. P gives Q and R each as many candies as they already have. After this, R gives Q half as many candies as Q already has, and R also gives P twice as many candies as P already has. Now each of them has the same number of candies with them. What is the ratio of the respective number of candies P and R had initially?
questions.questionHtml: P, Q and R together have 180 candies among them. P gives Q and R each as many candies as they already have. After this, R gives Q half as many candies as Q already has, and R also gives P twice as many candies as P already has. Now each of them has the same number of candies with them. What is the ratio of the respective number of candies P and R had initially?
questions.solution:
Given: p + q + r = 180

Step 1: P gives Q and R as many candies as they already have

→ Q = q + q = 2q

→ R = r + r = 2r

→ P = p – (q + r)

Step 2: R gives Q half of Q’s current (2q) → gives q

→ Q = 2q + q = 3q

→ R = 2r – q

Then R gives P twice of P’s current (p – q – r)

→ gives 2(p – q – r)

→ P = p – (q + r) + 2(p – q – r) = 3p – 3q – 3r

→ R = [2r – q] – 2(p – q – r) = 4r + q – 2p

Final values: P = 3p – 3q – 3r

Q = 3q

R = 4r + q – 2p

All equal ⇒ set P = Q and P = R

Equation 1: 3p – 3q – 3r = 3q

⇒ 3p = 6q + 3r

⇒ p = 2q + r

Equation 2: 3p – 3q – 3r = 4r + q – 2p ⇒ 5p = 4q + 7r

Substitute p = 2q + r into Equation 2: 5(2q + r) = 4q + 7r

⇒ 10q + 5r = 4q + 7r

⇒ 6q = 2r ⇒ r = 3q

Then p = 2q + r = 2q + 3q = 5q

Required ratio: P : R = p : r = 5q : 3q = 5 : 3
